claim_statement_pin: Sheaf/cohomological obstruction measures may identify cross-source climate-data inconsistencies or coverage defects not captured as efficiently by simpler graph and residual diagnostics.
realization_rule: Open obligations are permitted. A realized obligation requires executable witnesses. The overall method must not be described as realized sheaf cohomology while any required structural obligation remains open.

obligations.statement: A finite simplicial complex and cochain groups over an explicit coefficient field are constructed from declared simplices.
Coboundary maps are linear over the coefficient field and satisfy d_(k+1) o d_k = 0 on the reference complex.
Betti numbers are computed as dimensions of cohomology groups and agree with known finite-complex fixtures.
For a declared finite cover of a discrete support set, nerve simplices are constructed exactly from non-empty common intersections.
A finite cellular sheaf can carry non-constant finite-dimensional stalks with explicit restriction maps whose composition is checked as a hard invariant.
Station simplices are derived from a scientifically declared geographic coverage/intersection rule rather than arbitrary station tuples.
A concrete climate-data stalk model and restriction maps are defined with units and missing-data semantics.
Identity and composition laws for the actual climate-data restrictions are executable invariants.
The climate-data cochain differential is constructed from the declared restriction maps and independently satisfies d^2 = 0.
Compatibility, existence, and uniqueness semantics for global sections are implemented against the actual restrictions.
Known-topology, injected-fault, withheld-data, and negative-control experiments test whether the sheaf quantities detect what they claim to detect.
Task-scoped real-data evaluation demonstrates incremental value, if any, over graph residual, QC, interpolation, and other declared baselines.
